CMB lensing visualizer

The CMB constrains cosmological parameters mostly through the observed pattern of anisotropies at the epoch of recombination, z*≃1100. However, the photons used to measure these anisotropies are deflected by fluctuations in the matter density along the line of sight, altering the pattern we observe. Given a set of cosmological parameters, ΛCDM predicts how strongly the primary anisotropies should be distorted. This effect is referred to as CMB lensing. Deflections smear power between neighboring multipoles, smoothing the peaks and troughs in the standard 2–pt spectra CℓTT,TE,EE.

One way to attempt to remove the lensing information is to rescale it, replacing CLΦΦ by ALCLΦΦ in the calculation of the lensed 2–pt function. A more general approach for separating out lensing information was presented by Motloch and Hu. Instead of a uniform rescaling, they decompose the lensing power spectrum into its principal components (PCs), CLΦΦ=CL,fidΦΦexp{∑i=1NPCKL(i)Θ(i)}, where CL,fidΦΦ is a fixed fiducial lensing power spectrum, KL(i) are orthonormal modes ordered by how much information they contain about power spectra peak–smoothing, and Θ(i) are the coefficients of these PCs. Because CL,fidΦΦ is fixed, the lensing that smooths the peaks no longer depends on the cosmological parameters. We take CL,fidΦΦ to be the lensing spectrum at the posterior mean of the unlensed CMB. In the equation below, ℒ is the lensing operation, which takes an unlensed spectrum and a lensing potential and returns the lensed spectrum, and p are the cosmological parameters.
